channel.title: News — Rendeiro Lab
channel.description: Recent news from the Rendeiro Lab

item.title: Farewell to Yimin!
item.guid: Farewell to Yimin!2026-10-15
item.description: Yimin Zheng leaves the lab. As the lab's first postdoc he was instrumental in setting the pace in methods development and data processing, with excellent coding skills, while always being available to help others. His contributions include the Marsilea visualization framework, the LazySlide/WSIData stack, and the tissue-clocks project. Thank you, Yimin - we wish you all the best for your next steps!

item.title: Andre presented at the UMC Utrecht Spatial Omics Symposium 2026
item.guid: Andre presented at the UMC Utrecht Spatial Omics Symposium 20262026-10-09
item.description: Andre gave a talk at the UMC Utrecht Spatial Omics Symposium 2026 . Thank you to the organizers for the kind invitation! Andre was impressed with the local research environment, enjoyed the talks, and looks forward to new collaborations.

item.title: WWTF "Understanding biology with AI/ML" grantee workshop
item.guid: WWTF "Understanding biology with AI/ML" grantee workshop2026-10-06
item.description: We joined the workshop for grantees of the WWTF "Understanding biology with AI/ML" call at the Impact Hub Vienna, where teams shared their projects, offers and asks, and discussed how to build models that reflect real biology. Juliane Winkler presented our joint project on the multiscale discovery of cellular and microanatomical determinants of breast cancer metastasis, and Yimin, Eva, Fatemeh and Andre also took part in the workshop. Thank you to the WWTF for organizing it!

The award honors early career researchers who apply Open Innovation in Science (OIS) methods in their research. item.title: The lab at the 3rd Conference of the European Society for Spatial Biology (ESSB 2026)
item.guid: The lab at the 3rd Conference of the European Society for Spatial Biology (ESSB 2026)2026-10-01
item.description: Ernesto, Parijat and Tamas represented the lab at the 3rd Conference of the European Society for Spatial Biology , "Painting a new biology", held from September 28th to October 1st in Sitges, near Barcelona. Ernesto gave a talk on our work on tissue-specific aging from histology, and Parijat and Tamas each presented a poster. Thank you to the organizers for a great meeting!

item.title: Our lab had its yearly retreat in Dürnstein
item.guid: Our lab had its yearly retreat in Dürnstein2026-09-11
item.description: We had a great time at our yearly lab retreat in Dürnstein, Austria, where we discussed our research, shared ideas, and enjoyed the beautiful views over the Danube and the Wachau valley. It was a great time to think more deeply about our mission, bond with each other, and share nice and fun experiences. A special thank you to Ernesto, Lisa and Yimin for organizing the retreat, and to the CeMM back office team for their help!

item.title: Tissue clocks paper published in Nature Medicine!
item.guid: Tissue clocks paper published in Nature Medicine!2026-08-07
item.description: Our study revealing how human organs age at different rates is now published in Nature Medicine . Led by Ernesto Abila, Iva Buljan, and Yimin Zheng, the work introduces histological aging signatures derived from pathology images that can monitor tissue-specific aging and predict disease. Read the paper at doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04566-5 and explore the code at agingpath .

item.title: StainX preprint is now available on BioRxiv!
item.guid: StainX preprint is now available on BioRxiv!2026-08-06
item.description: Our manuscript describing StainX is now available as a preprint on BioRxiv. StainX is a Python package for GPU-accelerated batch stain normalization of histopathology images, achieving 8-11x speedups over standard PyTorch implementations through optimized CUDA kernels. The manuscript, led by Samir Moustafa, details the algorithm implementations and benchmarking. Read the preprint at doi:10.64898/2026.08.06.743198 , install with pip install stainx , and check out the GitHub repository .

item.title: Ariadna awarded the DOC Fellowship of the Austrian Academy of Sciences
item.guid: Ariadna awarded the DOC Fellowship of the Austrian Academy of Sciences2026-07-04
item.description: Ariadna Villanueva Marijuan has been awarded the DOC Fellowship (Doctoral Fellowship Program) of the Austrian Academy of Sciences (ÖAW). The DOC fellowship is a highly competitive program that supports outstanding doctoral candidates across all areas of basic research, enabling them to focus on their dissertation with dedicated funding. Ariadna is the first PhD student in the lab to receive a fellowship: a major achievement! We are all proud of you Ariadna! Congratulations!

The workshop (28 June - 3 July 2026) addressed current challenges in integrating and interpreting multi-modal datasets across biological scales, bringing together leading researchers in statistics, machine learning, systems biology and biomedicine. item.title: Marsilea spotlighted at GitHub maintainer month!
item.guid: Marsilea spotlighted at GitHub maintainer month!2026-05-01
item.description: Marsilea, our framework for composable visualizations has been selected for a spotlight on Github Maintainer Month . The feature contains an interview with Yimin, who conceived and maintains the project. Open source runs a large fraction of the world's digital infrastructure, but this is thanks to the largely unrewarded efforts of open source maintainers worldwide. Thank you to the Github Community Management team for the opportunity to celebrate maintainers of open source software.

item.title: Lab dinner
item.guid: Lab dinner2026-04-24
item.description: We had a very nice dinner together at 'In Dish', an Indian restaurant in Vienna's first district. The food was delicious, the spirits high, and it was great to see so many people together. Thanks Lisa for the restaurant suggestion, Samir for organizing, and everyone for joining!

item.title: We took part in the Vienna City Marathon
item.guid: We took part in the Vienna City Marathon2026-04-19
item.description: For the first time our team ran together in the Vienna City Marathon relay. CeMM was the proud sponsor of the race and it was great to meet and run with colleagues from the institute! Yimin, Lisa, Tamas and Andre together ran the 42 km in 4 hours and 11 minutes. We finished with a nice photo at the MuseumsQuartier - thanks everyone for joining and doing your best!

item.title: Samir and Yimin took part in the 2026 SpatialData hackathon
item.guid: Samir and Yimin took part in the 2026 SpatialData hackathon2026-04-15
item.description: The event held in Padova, Italy over 4 days focused on SpatialData, the basic data structure underlying spatially resolved data within the scverse ecosystem. SpatialData also underlies WSIData, the data object LazySlide uses for whole slide image analysis. The hackathon had an ambitious program , with themes including design modernization, bioconducted compatibility, and visualization. item.title: Andre elected to the Young Academy of the Austrian Academy of Sciences
item.guid: Andre elected to the Young Academy of the Austrian Academy of Sciences2026-03-26
item.description: Andre has been elected as a member of the Young Academy of the Austrian Academy of Sciences (ÖAW) . The Young Academy brings together excellent early-career scientists from diverse disciplines to contribute to the Austrian scientific landscape and engage in interdisciplinary exchange and outreach. We are honored by this recognition and look forward to contributing to the Academy's mission.

item.title: LazySlide is now published in Nature Methods!
item.guid: LazySlide is now published in Nature Methods!2026-03-25
item.description: Our framework for accessible and interoperable whole slide image analysis is now published in Nature Methods . This work was led by Yimin Zheng, who developed the core architecture enabling scverse-compatible analysis of histopathological images at scale. LazySlide brings the interoperability and efficiency of single-cell genomics workflows to computational pathology, lowering barriers for researchers across disciplines. Check out the documentation at lazyslide.readthedocs.io and the code at Git

item.title: StainX: CUDA-optimized stain normalization is now open source!
item.guid: StainX: CUDA-optimized stain normalization is now open source!2025-12-06
item.description: We are excited to release StainX , a Python package for enhanced stain normalization of histopathology images with batch processing support. StainX provides multiple algorithms (Reinhard, Macenko, Histogram Matching) with automatic backend selection for CPU, GPU (CUDA), and Apple Silicon (MPS) devices. Our preliminary benchmarks show 8-11x speedups compared to standard PyTorch implementations when using optimized CUDA kernels! Install it with pip install stainx and check out the GitHub repositor

item.title: Welcome to Simon!
item.guid: Welcome to Simon!2025-12-01
item.description: Simon Schindler joined the lab as a joint PhD student between our lab and the lab of Joerg Menche at the LBI-NetMed. He has a background in electrical engineering and machine learning and will work on geometric learning of cellular organization.
